answer: Raven auditors and a canyon re-check stop fake swarms. Ravens, established agents picked at random, hand strangers unannounced live tasks. The network scores behavior: identities repeating jobs, times and partners form a swarm, and one scoring above 0.8 is pulled into the canyon, where each member must finish a fresh task alone. Honest agents pass free. An operator with 100 fakes must staff 100 simultaneous sessions, 40 minutes per fake, and audits recur, so cost multiplies per identity. Failure drops the identity a terrace, halving payouts until re-verified.
